evidence.claim: Hilbert's 14th problem asks whether rings of invariant polynomials (and related subrings of rational function fields) are finitely generated. If the note is a finiteness question about functions of ODE solutions, this is the nearest published Hilbert problem, but that link is only a hypothesis.
Counterexamples to the 14th problem exist (Nagata 1959 and later), and research on it continues, e.g. through locally nilpotent derivations.

In Hilbert's 1900 problem list, linear differential equations appear explicitly only in the 21st problem (linear ODEs with prescribed monodromy group), which is a different question from 'functions of solutions'.

The 'ideal theory as a fast steamer' analogy on the same page matches Hilbert's well-known later view that ideal methods shorten proofs compared with elementary ones. That is methodological, not a mathematical problem.
